The Oyo State Government on Monday commenced the verification exercise for property owners affected in Segment 2 of the Ibadan Circular Road project. The development follows the directive of Governor Seyi Makinde that all eligible claimants and property owners affected by the project should be compensated. The Chairman of the Verification Exercise and Executive Assistant to the Governor on Security Matters, CP Sunday Odukoya (retd.), disclosed this during the exercise held at the Secretariat, Agodi, Ibadan. This was contained in a statement issued by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media, Sulaimon Olarenwaju, in Ibadan, the state capital. Addressing the affected property owners alongside the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, Wasiu Olatunbosun, Odukoya stated that the government had successfully concluded the first segment of the exercise and had now commenced the second segment. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He also warned beneficiaries to be wary of individuals falsely presenting themselves as agents of the government. The governor’s aide stressed that the state government had not appointed any agent, coordinator or representative to liaise with beneficiaries, noting that the activities of such individuals could create confusion, delay genuine claimants and encourage fraudulent practices. Odukoya explained that the number of persons to be verified in the second segment would depend on turnout, noting that some individuals captured under the first segment who initially doubted that compensation would be paid were now coming forward for verification. On the requirements for verification, he stated that affected persons were expected to present their land title documents, National Identification Number, passport photographs and an affidavit affirming ownership of the property. Speaking with journalists shortly after briefing the affected property owners, Odukoya said beneficiaries had been sensitised on the need to maintain discipline and orderliness throughout the exercise, adding that priority attention would be given to elderly persons. He reassured affected property owners of the government’s commitment to providing relief to all genuine claimants and ensuring transparency throughout the process. “We are conducting this verification exercise as directed by the governor so that everyone receives their rightful entitlement. “We have completed the first segment, and this is the second segment. Some of those captured in the first segment who did not believe the compensation would be paid are now coming forward. However, we have assured them that their cases will be attended to immediately after we conclude the second segment. “We have informed them about the requirements for the exercise, including their property deeds, NIN, passport photographs and an affidavit confirming ownership of the land. “We have also advised them to remain disciplined and orderly throughout the exercise, especially because there are elderly people among them who are being given priority attention. “The government of Governor Seyi Makinde remains committed to ensuring that every genuine claimant receives his or her rightful compensation. We want all affected property owners to be assured that the process will be transparent, fair and beneficial to all concerned,” Odukoya said. Ademola Adegbite
